chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces one non-existent instruction ("release its phase") with another claim that this diff never establishes: the new reason says `` `ddflow unblock <phase id>` releases a whole phase``. The bug report this change is supposed to fix states that `ddflow unblock` "takes exactly one item id (usage: ddflow unblock [--note] id) and there is no phase-level release anywhere in `ddflow --help`." The diff touches only the reason string and a test; it adds no phase-level release and provides no evidence that passing a phase id to `unblock` cascades to release the held children. Given the reported environment (`archive_globs` matching `docs/todo.md`, task `159.A.1` held with reason "in an archive file"), an agent that follows the new advice and runs `ddflow unblock 159.A` will, if `unblock` acts on the single id it is given, leave `159.A.1` still held — the exact failure the bug describes, just reworded. The fix is only correct if `unblock <phase>` is actually recursive, which nothing in the change shows or tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test claims the advice "works as written" (`# the advice works as written`) but the only assertion on that path is `run_cli(repo, "unblock", "159.A")[0] == OK`, i.e. the CLI exited 0. It never checks `_state(repo).items["159.A.1"].state` (or that its `blocked_reason` cleared), so the test passes whether `unblock 159.A` actually releases the held subtree or merely no-ops/returns success while `159.A.1` stays held. Because the whole point of the bug is that the printed advice must be actionable, the regression test does not protect against the failure it is supposed to guard: a `unblock` implementation that accepts the phase id but does not drive the archived task would keep this test green while the bug remains live.

chunk_findings.detail: The change only rewrites the hold string; it adds no phase-level release anywhere in the command layer. Yet the new text — ``ddflow unblock <phase id>` releases a whole phase`` — advertises exactly that capability, and the bug report this change claims to fix explicitly states that `ddflow unblock` takes a single item id and that "there is no phase-level release anywhere in `ddflow --help`". So the fix replaces one unactionable instruction ("release its phase") with another instruction whose validity the change never establishes: nothing in the diff makes `unblock <phase id>` cascade to a phase's held tasks. The only new test does not actually check that following the advice works — it asserts `run_cli(repo, "unblock", "159.A")[0] == OK` and never inspects the state of `159.A.1`, the item that carries the reason. Given input `docs/todo.md` in `archive_globs` with a held task `159.A.1` whose hold is recorded per item at import, a command that flips only the phase item (or returns OK without recursing into children) would satisfy the test while leaving `159.A.1` held, i.e. the reported 791 held tasks would still not be driveable by the advice printed in their reason. To guard the fix, the test needs to assert that `159.A.1` (and the subtree) actually leaves HOLD after the call, not merely that the invocation exits 0.
